title: ABCG2
text: Gene: ABCG2 (ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 2 (Breast Cancer Resistance Protein, BCRP)). Functional category: Drug transport / chemoresistance. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Efflux pump and cancer stem cell marker; high expression in OSCC side-population cells associates with resistance to cisplatin, 5-FU and other agents and with poorer outcome. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Drug transport / metabolism. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.63 (*), methotrexate fold change 0.49 (**); control = 1.0.

title: SPP1
text: Gene: SPP1 (Secreted phosphoprotein 1 (Osteopontin)). Functional category: ECM / signalling. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Overexpressed in OSCC tumours and serum; promotes invasion, migration and metastasis via integrin/CD44 signalling and is linked to nodal metastasis and poor prognosis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, ECM remodelling & invasion. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: CXCL8
text: Gene: CXCL8 (C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (Interleukin-8)). Functional category: Chemokine / inflammation. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Elevated in OSCC tissue and saliva (candidate salivary biomarker); drives angiogenesis, proliferation, invasion and EMT, and contributes to chemoresistance. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, Inflammation & cytokines, Angiogenesis. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: CXCL12
text: Gene: CXCL12 (C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12 (Stromal cell-derived factor-1, SDF-1)). Functional category: Chemokine / microenvironment. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Ligand for CXCR4; the CXCL12–CXCR4 axis promotes OSCC cell migration, invasion and lymph node metastasis; largely produced by cancer-associated fibroblasts. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, Inflammation & cytokines, ECM remodelling & invasion. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: BAX
text: Gene: BAX (BCL2-associated X protein). Functional category: Apoptosis (pro-apoptotic). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Mediator of mitochondrial apoptosis induced by cisplatin and radiation; reduced BAX or a low BAX/BCL2 ratio is associated with treatment resistance in OSCC. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Apoptosis. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 1.75 (***), methotrexate fold change 6.73 (****); control = 1.0.

title: PDGFB
text: Gene: PDGFB (Platelet-derived growth factor subunit B). Functional category: Growth factor. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Supports tumour–stroma crosstalk, angiogenesis and fibroblast recruitment; PDGF signalling is upregulated in OSCC and linked to invasion and metastasis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Receptor tyrosine kinase, Angiogenesis. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.59 (**), methotrexate fold change 1.01 (ns); control = 1.0.

title: SLC7A5
text: Gene: SLC7A5 (Solute carrier family 7 member 5 (L-type amino acid transporter 1, LAT1)). Functional category: Amino acid transport / metabolism. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Overexpressed in OSCC; supplies leucine for mTORC1-driven growth and is an independent marker of poor prognosis; investigated as a therapeutic target. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Drug transport / metabolism. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.19 (**), methotrexate fold change 1.21 (*); control = 1.0. DISCREPANCY: Sheet 2 says downregulated; Fig. 6 is drug-dependent (opposite for one drug).

title: ANXA1
text: Gene: ANXA1 (Annexin A1). Functional category: Inflammation / membrane signalling. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Expression is frequently reduced in OSCC versus normal mucosa and loss correlates with poor differentiation; also implicated in modulating chemosensitivity. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Inflammation & cytokines. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: BRAF
text: Gene: BRAF (B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase). Functional category: MAPK signalling kinase. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Activating mutations are rare in OSCC (unlike melanoma), but BRAF is a component of the EGFR–RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK proliferation pathway active in these tumours. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: MAPK/RAS-RAF-ERK. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.1 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.51 (***); control = 1.0.

title: ERBB2
text: Gene: ERBB2 (Erb-b2 receptor tyrosine kinase 2 (HER2/neu)). Functional category: Receptor tyrosine kinase. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Overexpression/amplification reported in a subset of OSCC; associated with aggressive behaviour and may contribute to resistance to EGFR-targeted therapy. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: MAPK/RAS-RAF-ERK, Receptor tyrosine kinase. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.15 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.15 (**); control = 1.0.

title: SRC
text: Gene: SRC (SRC proto-oncogene, non-receptor tyrosine kinase). Functional category: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Frequently activated in head and neck SCC; promotes invasion, migration and EMT and contributes to resistance to EGFR inhibitors and chemotherapy. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: MAPK/RAS-RAF-ERK, Receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.5 (**), methotrexate fold change 0.45 (*); control = 1.0.

title: TP53
text: Gene: TP53 (Tumour protein p53). Functional category: Tumour suppressor / DNA damage response. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): The most frequently mutated gene in OSCC (often >60-70%); mutation is linked to tobacco exposure, genomic instability, poor prognosis and reduced response to cisplatin and radiation. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Apoptosis, Cell cycle, DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 1.09 (ns), methotrexate fold change 2.27 (****); control = 1.0.

title: BRCA1
text: Gene: BRCA1 (BRCA1 DNA repair associated (Breast cancer type 1 susceptibility protein)). Functional category: DNA repair (homologous recombination). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Its expression influences sensitivity to platinum drugs and PARP inhibitors; altered BRCA1 expression has been reported in OSCC and linked to chemoresponse. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 1.61 (**), methotrexate fold change 1.76 (**); control = 1.0. DISCREPANCY: Sheet 2 says downregulated; Fig. 6 shows upregulation with both DTX and MTX.

title: ATM
text: Gene: ATM (ATM serine/threonine kinase (Ataxia telangiectasia mutated)). Functional category: DNA damage response kinase. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Senses DNA double-strand breaks and activates p53/CHK2; polymorphisms and altered expression are associated with OSCC risk and with radio- and chemosensitivity. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 1.44 (**), methotrexate fold change 1.98 (***); control = 1.0.

title: CDK2
text: Gene: CDK2 (Cyclin-dependent kinase 2). Functional category: Cell cycle. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Drives G1/S transition with cyclin E/A; elevated activity in OSCC supports uncontrolled proliferation and is associated with poor prognosis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Cell cycle. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.38 (**), methotrexate fold change 0.77 (*); control = 1.0.

title: PARP1
text: Gene: PARP1 (Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1). Functional category: DNA repair (base excision / single-strand break). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Upregulated in OSCC; repairs chemotherapy-induced DNA damage and so contributes to cisplatin resistance; PARP inhibitors are being explored as sensitisers. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.36 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.62 (**); control = 1.0.

title: MLH1
text: Gene: MLH1 (MutL homolog 1). Functional category: DNA mismatch repair. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Reduced expression or promoter hypermethylation occurs in some OSCC; MMR deficiency is linked to tolerance of cisplatin-induced DNA damage. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: XRCC2
text: Gene: XRCC2 (X-ray repair cross-complementing 2). Functional category: DNA repair (homologous recombination). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): RAD51 paralog in double-strand break repair; polymorphisms have been studied for association with oral cancer risk and radiosensitivity. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: XRCC1
text: Gene: XRCC1 (X-ray repair cross-complementing 1). Functional category: DNA repair (base excision). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Scaffold protein for base excision/SSB repair; Arg399Gln and other polymorphisms are associated with OSCC risk (especially with tobacco) and treatment response. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.18 (****), methotrexate fold change 0.32 (***); control = 1.0.

title: GSK3B
text: Gene: GSK3B (Glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta). Functional category: Kinase / Wnt & PI3K signalling. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Inactivated downstream of AKT; loss of GSK3B activity stabilises beta-catenin and Snail, promoting EMT and invasion in OSCC. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: STAT3
text: Gene: STAT3 (Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3). Functional category: Transcription factor / JAK-STAT. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Constitutively activated in OSCC (via IL-6, EGFR); promotes proliferation, survival, immune evasion and cisplatin resistance; a candidate therapeutic target. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: JAK/STAT, Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, Immune evasion & antigen presentation, Transcription factors (AP-1 / MYC / STAT). Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: CYP2E1
text: Gene: CYP2E1 (Cytochrome P450 family 2 subfamily E member 1). Functional category: Xenobiotic metabolism. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Metabolises ethanol and tobacco nitrosamines to reactive carcinogens; polymorphisms are associated with oral cancer susceptibility, particularly in drinkers and smokers. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Drug transport / metabolism. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: JUN
text: Gene: JUN (Jun proto-oncogene, AP-1 transcription factor subunit (c-Jun)). Functional category: Transcription factor (AP-1). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): AP-1 component activated by JNK; promotes proliferation, invasion and MMP expression in OSCC and is involved in stress and chemotherapy responses. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: MAPK/RAS-RAF-ERK, Transcription factors (AP-1 / MYC / STAT). Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: AKT1
text: Gene: AKT1 (AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (Protein kinase B)). Functional category: PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): PI3K/AKT pathway is among the most frequently activated in OSCC; AKT1 drives survival, proliferation and resistance to chemotherapy and radiation. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: PI3K/AKT/mTOR. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: MYC
text: Gene: MYC (MYC proto-oncogene, bHLH transcription factor (c-Myc)). Functional category: Transcription factor / oncogene. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Amplified or overexpressed in a subset of OSCC; drives proliferation and metabolic reprogramming and is associated with poor prognosis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Cell cycle, Transcription factors (AP-1 / MYC / STAT). Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.21 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.27 (***); control = 1.0.

title: AURKA
text: Gene: AURKA (Aurora kinase A). Functional category: Mitosis / cell cycle. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Overexpressed in OSCC; associated with genomic instability, metastasis, poor survival and chemoresistance; Aurora kinase inhibitors are under investigation. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Cell cycle. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.08 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.93 (ns); control = 1.0.

title: ERCC1
text: Gene: ERCC1 (ERCC excision repair 1, endonuclease non-catalytic subunit). Functional category: DNA repair (nucleotide excision). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Key repair of cisplatin DNA adducts; high ERCC1 expression is associated with cisplatin resistance and poorer outcome in head and neck/oral SCC. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: XPC
text: Gene: XPC (XPC complex subunit, DNA damage recognition and repair factor). Functional category: DNA repair (global genome NER). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Recognises bulky DNA lesions, including tobacco carcinogen adducts; polymorphisms are associated with oral cancer risk and may influence platinum response. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 2.03 (****), methotrexate fold change 2.22 (****); control = 1.0. DISCREPANCY: Sheet 2 says downregulated; Fig. 6 shows upregulation with both DTX and MTX.

title: TNF
text: Gene: TNF (Tumour necrosis factor (TNF-alpha)). Functional category: Cytokine / inflammation. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Elevated in OSCC tissue and saliva; chronic TNF signalling via NF-kB promotes inflammation, invasion and EMT; polymorphisms linked to susceptibility. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, Inflammation & cytokines. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: CDKN1A
text: Gene: CDKN1A (Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A (p21, WAF1/CIP1)). Functional category: Cell cycle inhibitor. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): p53 target that mediates cell-cycle arrest after DNA damage; altered expression in OSCC is associated with prognosis and with response to chemotherapy. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Apoptosis, Cell cycle, DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 1.28 (*), methotrexate fold change 1.11 (ns); control = 1.0.

title: GSTM1
text: Gene: GSTM1 (Glutathione S-transferase mu 1). Functional category: Phase II detoxification. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Detoxifies tobacco carcinogens and some chemotherapy drugs; the GSTM1 null genotype is associated with increased oral cancer risk in tobacco users. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Drug transport / metabolism. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: MMP2
text: Gene: MMP2 (Matrix metallopeptidase 2 (Gelatinase A)). Functional category: ECM degradation / invasion. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Degrades type IV collagen of the basement membrane; overexpression in OSCC correlates with invasion depth, lymph node metastasis and poor prognosis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: ECM remodelling & invasion. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: MSH2
text: Gene: MSH2 (MutS homolog 2). Functional category: DNA mismatch repair. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Core MMR protein; altered expression is reported in OSCC and premalignant lesions and may influence cisplatin sensitivity. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 2.66 (****), methotrexate fold change 3.23 (****); control = 1.0. DISCREPANCY: Sheet 2 says downregulated; Fig. 6 shows upregulation with both DTX and MTX.

title: CYP1A1
text: Gene: CYP1A1 (Cytochrome P450 family 1 subfamily A member 1). Functional category: Xenobiotic metabolism. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Activates polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons from tobacco smoke into DNA-binding carcinogens; polymorphisms are associated with OSCC risk. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Drug transport / metabolism. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: RAD51
text: Gene: RAD51 (RAD51 recombinase). Functional category: DNA repair (homologous recombination). Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Central HR protein; overexpression in OSCC enhances repair of chemo- and radiation-induced DNA damage and is associated with resistance. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: DNA repair & damage response. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.31 (**), methotrexate fold change 0.49 (**); control = 1.0.

title: CCR5
text: Gene: CCR5 (C-C motif chemokine receptor 5). Functional category: Chemokine receptor / immune. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Receptor for CCL5 (RANTES); the CCL5–CCR5 axis promotes OSCC cell migration, invasion and metastasis and shapes immune infiltration. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Inflammation & cytokines, Immune evasion & antigen presentation. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: HLA-C
text: Gene: HLA-C (Major histocompatibility complex, class I, C). Functional category: Antigen presentation / immune. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Presents tumour antigens to T cells and regulates NK cells; downregulation of HLA class I in OSCC is a mechanism of immune escape. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Immune evasion & antigen presentation. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: MAPK1
text: Gene: MAPK1 (Mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (ERK2)). Functional category: MAPK signalling kinase. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Terminal kinase of the EGFR–RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK pathway; frequently activated in OSCC and drives proliferation and survival. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: MAPK/RAS-RAF-ERK. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.56 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.11 (***); control = 1.0.

title: MAPK8
text: Gene: MAPK8 (Mitogen-activated protein kinase 8 (JNK1)). Functional category: Stress-activated MAPK. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Activated by stress and cisplatin; context-dependent roles in OSCC including apoptosis induction and promotion of invasion via c-Jun/AP-1. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: MAPK/RAS-RAF-ERK, Apoptosis. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: SLC10A1
text: Gene: SLC10A1 (Solute carrier family 10 member 1 (Sodium/taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide, NTCP)). Functional category: Bile acid transport. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Mainly hepatic; little established role in OSCC. Relevance here is likely as a drug-uptake transporter or exploratory candidate. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Drug transport / metabolism. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.59 (*), methotrexate fold change 1.8 (***); control = 1.0. DISCREPANCY: Sheet 2 says downregulated; Fig. 6 is drug-dependent (opposite for one drug). Exploratory: the sheet notes little established OSCC role for this gene.

title: AXL
text: Gene: AXL (AXL receptor tyrosine kinase). Functional category: Receptor tyrosine kinase. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Overexpressed in OSCC; promotes EMT, invasion and metastasis and mediates resistance to EGFR inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors and cisplatin. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, ECM remodelling & invasion. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: IGF1R

title: PTEN

Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: PI3K/AKT/mTOR. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.54 (***), methotrexate fold change 0.51 (**); control = 1.0. DISCREPANCY: Sheet 2 says upregulated; Fig. 6 shows downregulation with both DTX and MTX.

title: TGM3
text: Gene: TGM3 (Transglutaminase 3). Functional category: Epithelial differentiation. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Involved in keratinocyte cornified envelope formation; frequently downregulated in OSCC, and loss is associated with poor differentiation and worse prognosis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: ECM remodelling & invasion. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: VEGFA
text: Gene: VEGFA (Vascular endothelial growth factor A). Functional category: Angiogenesis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Angiogenesis. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 0.29 (**), methotrexate fold change 0.71 (*); control = 1.0.

title: PIK3CA
text: Gene: PIK3CA (Phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit alpha (p110-alpha)). Functional category: PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling. title: CASP9

Sheet symbol 'CAS9' is not an official symbol; interpreted as CASP9.

title: IL6

Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: JAK/STAT, Wnt/beta-catenin & EMT, Inflammation & cytokines, Immune evasion & antigen presentation. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: COL1A2
text: Gene: COL1A2 (Collagen type I alpha 2 chain). Functional category: Extracellular matrix. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Upregulated in OSCC stroma (cancer-associated fibroblasts); contributes to matrix remodelling and invasion and is associated with poor prognosis. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: ECM remodelling & invasion. Not among the 29 genes measured by RT-PCR in the in-vitro paper (status comes from sheet 2 only).

title: CASP3

Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): DOWNREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Apoptosis. title: STAT5B

title: RB1
text: Gene: RB1 (RB transcriptional corepressor 1 (Retinoblastoma protein)). Functional category: Tumour suppressor / cell cycle. Role in OSCC (sheet 1, literature summary): Controls G1/S checkpoint; its pathway is commonly disrupted in OSCC (often via CDKN2A loss or CCND1 amplification), and HPV E7 inactivates pRb. Expected status after chemotherapy (sheet 2, the team's study): UPREGULATED. Pathways/processes: Cell cycle. Measured by RT-PCR in KB cells (in-vitro paper, Fig. 6): docetaxel fold change 1.07 (ns), methotrexate fold change 1.43 (**); control = 1.0.

title: MMP7

title: Drug study overview
text: In-vitro paper (Natesan et al., Cell Biochemistry and Biophysics 2025): KB oral cancer cells were treated with docetaxel (DTX, 1.5-50 nM) and methotrexate (MTX, 25-250 uM). MTT assay IC50 at 24 h: DTX 6.25 nM, MTX 100 uM. In-silico part: DisGeNET gave 773 OSCC-related genes; SwissTargetPrediction gave 82 DTX/MTX target genes; 18 genes overlap OSCC with DTX and 18 with MTX; 25 further literature genes were added (43 genes) for ShinyGO enrichment and STRING/Cytoscape CytoHubba hub-gene analysis. RT-PCR measured 29 genes; western blots showed increased caspases 3, 7 and 9; DNA fragmentation increased; wound-healing migration and colony formation decreased. Authors conclude DTX showed a significantly stronger cytotoxic effect than MTX.

Surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy are common treatment modalities for oral cancer. Chemotherapeutic drugs are effective in treating cancers; however, they also have various side effects that can affect patient survival rates. Docetaxel (DTX) and methotrexate (MTX) are used to treat multiple solid tumors. However, there are limited reports available on the efficacy of these drugs against oral cancer. Thus, in the present study, we investigated the effect of DTX and MTX as monotherapies on KB oral cancer cell lines. Initially, functional enrichment, gene ontology, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were performed to understand the key biological processes and interaction networks associated with DTX- and MTX-targeted genes in oral carcinoma. In vitro analyses were conducted in KB cells treated with different concentrations of DTX (1.5–50 nM) and MTX (25 to 250µM) to identify the effective

title: In-vitro paper p.1
text: th DTX- and MTX-targeted genes in oral carcinoma. In vitro analyses were conducted in KB cells treated with different concentrations of DTX (1.5–50 nM) and MTX (25 to 250µM) to identify the effective IC50 concentrations using MTT assay. Next, RT-PCR analysis was performed to evaluate the expression of 29 major genes involved in oral cancer, and apoptotic protein levels were analyzed using western blotting. DTX and MTX treatment resulted in significant upregulation of apoptotic and tumor suppressor genes, together with downregulation of oncogenes, drug transporters, growth factors, cell cycle regulators, and signal transduction genes. Western blot data showed that there was an increase in caspases (3,7, and 9) during DTX and MTX treatment in oral cancer cells. Moreover, enhanced DNA fragmentation, reduced cell migration, and decreased colony-forming ability have been observed. Overall, our data suggest that DTX showed a significant cytotoxic effect against oral cancer cells compared to MTX and could be used as an effective chemotherapeutic drug against oral cancer in the near future; however, extensive molecular investigations are still warranted. title: In-vitro paper p.2
text: Cell Biochemistry and Biophysics Cancer is characterized by uncontrolled cell growth, excessive cell proliferation, and impaired apoptosis. Cancer that develops in the lip and oral cavity is collectively referred to as oral cancer. According to GLOBOCAN, oral cancer is the most common form of head and neck cancer, with an incidence of 380,000 new cases of lip and oral cavity cancer and 180,000 deaths in 2020 [1]. Two–thirds of the oral cancer incidence was observed in developing countries, with India alone accounting for 100,000 cases annually [2]. Oral cancer is multifaceted and is associated with various genetic, epigenetic, habitual (alcohol/tobacco/betel nut chewing/ smoking), and microbial factors, which greatly differ with ethnic origin or geographical regions [3]. Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, and immunotherapy are common treatment modalities for oral cancer [4]. However, surgery remains the primary treatment option, along with radiotherapy or chemotherapy, administered as adjuvant treatment for patients with a high risk of recurrence. Chemotherapy or radiotherapy are inevitable therapeutic options for oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) when the patient is unfit for surgery [5]. The treatment for OSCC depends on multiple factors, such as tumor stage, location, and patient’s overall health status [6].

Cisplatin, carboplatin, 5-fluorouracil, hydroxyurea, paclitaxel, and docetaxel are FDA-approved drugs used for the treatment of oral cancer [1]. Platinum-based antineoplastic agents such as cisplatin and carboplatin block DNA replication. Taxane drugs such as paclitaxel and docetaxel interfere with mitotic spindle assembly, chromosome segregation, and cell division [7]. Docetaxel is a semisynthetic secondgeneration taxane-family chemotherapeutic agent that is primarily used to treat lung cancer, colorectal cancer, breast cancer, and HNSCC. Gupta et al. reported that a docetaxel nanoformulation (PLGA-Dtx) effectively reduced cell proliferation by G2/M cell cycle arrest and induced apoptosis and necroptosis by targeting the TNF-α/RIP1/RIP3 pathway in SCC-9 tongue squamous cell carcinoma [8]. Docetaxel promotes apoptosis by upregulating caspase expression and decreasing mitochondrial membrane potential via the interdependent MAPK-JNK, MAPK-ERK1/2, and AMPKα signalling pathways in tongue squamous cell carcinoma [9]. We highlighted the deregulations in key cellular signaling pathways, including PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK, Wnt/Beta-catenin, Notch, Hedgehog, Hippo-YAP/TAZ, and JAK/STAT, which contribute to tumor initiation, progression, and therapy resistance. In addition, we provided an overview of epigenetic mechanisms in HNSCC including DNA methylation changes, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA regulation. Emerging epigenetic therapeutic strategies under clinical investigation were also highlighted. Moreover, molecular and epigenetic signatures related to HPV-positive and HPV-negative HNSCC further emphasized the complexity and clinical heterogeneity of disease. Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a biologically complex malignancy characterized by molecular heterogeneity, high recurrence rate, and poor clinical outcome. A deeper understanding of the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying HNSCC is essential for improving early diagnosis, and therapy response providing a better patient stratification. An extensive review of current literature was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar which included 280 articles highlighting recent advancements in gene expression profiling in HNSCC. This review summarizes the complex molecular events in HNSCC emphasizing the key deregulations in cellular signaling pathways, differential gene expression regulated by epigenetic modifications.

HNSCC demonstrates aggressive behavior with limited treatment options especially in case of recurrent and metastatic tumors. Surgery is the first line treatment for HNSCC, but it is associated with challenges such as difficult surgical margins, trouble in speech and swallowing, physiological and social stress. Other treatment options include chemotherapy and radiotherapy and they have their own limitations including toxicity, drug intolerance, and therapeutic resistance (Ascione et al. 2025). Accumulating evidence suggests that the variability in therapy response and poor clinical outcome in HNSCC are driven by genetic, epigenetic, and etiological factors such as tobacco usage, alcohol consumption and HPV infection (Zohud et al. 2023). Hence, understanding the molecular basis of HNSCC is essential for improving the treatment outcome. In this context, the present review discussed the modifications in gene expression pattern correlated to major cellular signaling networks and epigenetic alterations associated with HNSCC pathogenesis. These alterations affect tumor behavior, progression and promotes resistance to conventional therapies. Hence, we further discussed the conventional treatment strategies and therapy resistance contributing to treatment failure and poor overall survival. By summarizing current knowledge and emerging evidences, this review provides an overview of complex molecular landscape of HNSCC. These insights may advance the understanding of cancer progression and improve patient outcome.

HNSCC is classified into four clinical stages I, II, III, and IV based on the progression of the disease. Stage I & II are considered as early stages of cancer and III & IV are considered as locally-advanced stages. Stage IV was further classified as IVa and IVb with a distant metastatic percentage of 20% & 24% respectively (Pisani et al. 2020). According to GLOBOCAN 2022 estimate, HNSCC accounts for about 940,000 new cases and 480,000 deaths annually worldwide (Sun et al. 2025). The incidence rate varies for different regions of the body such as 389,846 cases of lip and oral cavity cancers, 189,191 cases of laryngeal cancer, 120,434 cases of nasopharyngeal cancer, 106,400 cases of oropharyngeal cancer, 86,257 cases of hypopharyngeal cancer and 55,083 cases of salivary gland cancer (Barsouk et al. 2023). Males are more prone to develop HNSCC than females with an incidence ratio ranging from 2:1 to 4:1 (Hashim et al. 2019). Epigenetic gene regulation, including DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNA, is crucial for cellular homeostasis and is frequently disrupted in HNSCC (Nirmaladevi 2020). Histone modification is one of the important epigenetic signatures responsible for HNSCC development and progression. For instance, transcriptional inactivation of H3K4me2 histones was prevalent in OSCC when compared to normal tissue. Histone lysine methyltransferase KMT2D, potential driver gene of OSCC is also frequently altered and its over expression induces stem celllike characteristics and activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling (Rajendran et al. 2025). Targeted therapies to treat HNSCC are gaining attention in recent years including EGFR inhibitors, PI3K/ AKT/mTOR inhibitors, aurora kinase inhibitors and VEGF inhibitors. Despite the development of novel inhibitors, therapy resistance remains common in HNSCC patients mainly due to tumor aggressiveness, heterogeneity, drug over usage and causing damage to normal tissue (Ghosh et al. 2022). Hence, natural compounds such as luteolin, resveratrol, vitamin A are gaining attention in HNSCC treatment (Porcheri et al. 2019). 5,4’-dihydroxy-6,8-dimethoxy-7-Orhamnosyl flavones (DDR), extracted from Indigofera aspalathoides exhibited anti-proliferative, anti-invasive and anti-metastatic potential thereby modulating PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and β-catenin signaling pathways (Al-Saeedi and Rajendran 2024). HNSCC subtypes are highly distinct in their clinical, pathological and molecular behavior providing the tumor complexity. Hence, understanding the cellular signaling networks involved in the disease progression is the key for developing novel biomarkers and to improve the overall treatment outcome. text: Molecular Genetics and Genomics (2026) 301:90 PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway regulates cell growth, survival, proliferation, and disease pathogenesis (Porta et al. 2014). The pathway is activated by receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR, VEGFR, FGFR), GPCRs, cytokine receptors, and integrins. Phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) catalyzes the conversion of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-triphosphate (PIP3) promoting AKT phosphorylation through phosphorylation at Thr308 by 3-Phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDK1) and at Ser473 by mTORC2 (He et al. 2021). Phosphate and tensin homolog (PTEN) negatively regulate PI3K signaling by dephosphorylating PIP3 and regenerating PIP2 (Hoxhaj and Manning 2020). Activated AKT phosphorylates multiple downstream target proteins notably glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK3), tuberous sclerosis 2 (TSC2), caspase9, and PRAS40 (Zou et al. 2019). Aberrant activation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway is common across many cancers and frequently altered in breast, colorectal, lung, prostate, and head & neck cancer (Peng et al. 2022). In HNSCC, frequent alterations including PIK3CA mutations, PTEN loss, and CDKN2A inactivation, were observed in both HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors. However, the mechanism of pathway activation differs by HPV status. In HPV-positive HNSCC, viral E7 oncoprotein inactivates and degrades RB1 which enhances CDK4/6 mediated cell cycle progression. HPV-negative HNSCC commonly harbors CCND1 gene amplification or CDKN2A loss promoting CDK4/6-mediated Rb1 phosphorylation and cell cycle progression (Verhees et al. 2025). PIK3CA mutations are particularly high in HPV-positive tumors and are associated with cancer metastasis and high tumor mutational burden suggesting the biological differences between these subgroups (Bridgham et al. 2025).

Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK also called as Ras/Raf/MAPK signaling pathway is a central regulator of cell proliferation, differentiation and survival that is activated by receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), GPCRs, EGFR, VEGFR, stem cell growth factor receptors, and insulin-like growth factor receptor (Moon and Ro 2021). The binding of ligands such as growth factors, cytokines, and interleukins to receptor tyrosine kinase induces receptor dimerization and autophosphorylation of specific tyrosine residues on the C-terminus of the receptor. Membrane-bound inactive Ras-GDP is converted to active Ras-GTP recruits Raf kinases (ARAF, BRAF, CRAF) to the plasma membrane, and sequentially phosphorylates MEK1/2 and ERK1/2. Upon activation, ERK translocate to the nucleus thereby activating the downstream effector genes involved in cell proliferation, survival, motility, and angiogenesis (Santarpia et al. 2012). emphasizing pathway interdependence (Novoplansky et al. 2023). Therapeutic challenges associated with HNSCC remains an aggressive type of cancer that is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages of tumor development. Patients often develop therapeutic resistance and become unreactive to therapy (Alsahafi et al. 2019). Tumor heterogeneity could lead to molecular divergence causing resistance to most of the targeted therapies. Intratumor genetic diversity and the existence of sub-clonal cancer cell populations significantly influence the outcome of targeted therapies and facilitate disease progression (Mroz and Rocco 2017).
